defect_retired: line-keyed allowlist entries ('file.py:LINE') moved whenever an unrelated edit shifted a line, tripping the suite four times across this arc — once causing a red-suite commit (a716c30)

new_keying.form: file :: enclosing symbol :: whitespace-normalized match text -> COUNT
new_keying.line_independent_by_construction: line numbers are used only to FIND the enclosing symbol; no line number enters a key
new_keying.counts_included_because: co-located occurrences must not hide behind each other — see the masked-occurrence finding below

masked_occurrence_finding.statement: TWO lookup-default occurrences on ONE line. The line-keyed allowlist collapsed them to a single entry, so the class census under-counted by one and a second occurrence sat inside an allowlisted key unseen. The rekey exposes it: the A32 census is 27 occurrences across 27 keys where the old list carried 26 entries. Line-keying was not merely fragile — it was under-counting the class it gates
masked_occurrence_finding.dispositioned: NO — counted and located only, as the A32 brief requires

structural_guard: test_no_allowlist_key_is_line_positional fails the suite if any key embeds a line number — the rekey cannot silently regress

demonstrated_not_asserted.line_movement_unit: keys computed over a source and over the same source shifted by five lines are equal (test_keys_survive_line_movement_demonstrated)
demonstrated_not_asserted.line_movement_live: five blank lines injected into the real palette_flake_rig.py moved every subsequent line number; the source-scan gates PASSED (5 passed) where the line-keyed form failed four times; file restored, zero diff
demonstrated_not_asserted.negative_control: a new lookup-default injected into a measurement module made the gate FAIL, naming the symbol and the text rather than a line: "palette_flake_rig.py::declaration::.get('x', 0.5) (found 1, allowed 0)"; file restored, 41 passed

scope_decision_stated: the rekey covers the LIVE GATES (the two test allowlists that trip). Line-keyed DISPOSITION RECORDS (allowlist_dispositions, the four-state table, the closure computations) are historical records of what was measured, not gates: they do not trip, and per 2k they stand as what was committed. Not rekeyed, and the decision is stated rather than left implicit
